# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_001_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 1

**1:1** In the records of the twelve tribes of Israel it is written: There was a man named Joachim, exceedingly wealthy. He brought double offerings before the Lord God, saying within himself: "My abundance shall benefit all the people; my offering shall bring forgiveness for all the people, and my repentance before the Lord God shall be my atonement."

**1:2** When the great day of the Lord drew near, the children of Israel were bringing their offerings. Reuben stood before him and said, "It is not lawful for you to present your offerings first, because you have not made seed in Israel."

**1:3** Joachim was deeply grieved. He went to consult the records of the twelve tribes of the people, saying, "I will search the records to see whether I alone have not made seed in Israel." He searched and found that every righteous man had raised up offspring in Israel. He then recalled the patriarch Abraham — how in his last days God had given him a son, Isaac.

**1:4** Exceedingly grieved, Joachim did not return to his wife but went out into the wilderness. He pitched his tent there and fasted forty days and forty nights, saying within himself: "I will not go down for food or drink until the Lord my God visits me; prayer shall be my food and drink."

---

## Translator's Note

This opening chapter introduces Joachim's crisis of childlessness within the framework of Jewish covenant theology. The doubling of offerings (1:1) establishes his piety while the humiliation at the temple (1:2) sets the narrative in motion. The wilderness retreat echoes Elijah and Moses, framing Joachim as a figure of prayer awaiting divine intervention.
